question: A rare event has just happened. Was it a one-off, or is something hidden remembering?

defect.role: the main project's machine, with one hidden defect

clean.role: the same emitter with nothing hidden behind it

stepped.role: the hidden defect's own frequency doubled, from 0.3 to 0.6 radians per step

chipmaking.reads: pair dose for a two-photon resist: P(first photon) x P(a second within three steps | the first)

photons.reads: g2(tau) = P(click at 3 + tau | click at 3) / P(click at 3 + tau)

lasers.reads: a frequency step of the hidden partner (0.3 to 0.6 radians per step) moves the after-click record

cost.scope: Records per run of the model on a perfect device. A rewound run uses about three times the gates.

ibm.scope: Recount of raw counts saved on 11 November 2026. Programmed models on superconducting qubits: no photon, laser, resist or wafer was measured, and no unknown defect was diagnosed.
ibm.g2_scope: After-click rate from the rewound circuit over the plain click rate from the plain circuit, at steps 4, 5 and 6. Two different circuits of one job, so drift between them is not in the interval.

noise_model.model: depolarizing gate errors at the reported rates times one echo-fitted scale, and this job's own readout errors; no idle decoherence, crosstalk or drift

new_job.scope: A fresh job. Predictions were written before it ran, for the qubits and calibration of 11 November.

limits: The machine is a toy with two memory qubits. An exact classical filter answers every question here, and is the reference the circuits are checked against.
Rewinding runs a MODEL inside a quantum computer. It cannot rewind a real laser, quantum dot or wafer.
No speedup is claimed. A rewound run uses about three times the gates of a plain run.
On IBM hardware the answers keep their order and lose most of their gap; see ibm and noise_model.
